subject: 20270422-performance-slo-qualification-novaretail-cost-levers-followup
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Evan Turner <evan.turner@novaretail.com>, Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO qualification - post-call recap

Hi Evan / Sofia -

Thanks again for the call earlier - good to meet the Nova Retail platform team. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope a Dedicated pool and configuration that meets your latency SLOs and cost targets.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use: real-time product recommendations and upsell prompts for web & mobile.
- Peak concurrency: expected 150 concurrent sessions during promos, baseline 30-40.
- Throughput: ~120k reqs/day, concentrated in 2-3 hour windows.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end < 200ms for 1-2k token prompts, streaming allowed for large responses.
- Accuracy: you will tolerate a small quality delta for faster models if latency/cost are improved.

Open items / clarifying questions:
1) Can you confirm the 95th p95 target is end-to-end (app -> Redwood -> model -> first byte) or just model generation time?
2) Typical prompt lengths (tokens) for the recommendation flow - you mentioned 400-1,200 tokens; can you give a sample distribution (p50/p95)?
3) Do you need strict streaming for UI (first token within X ms) or is server-side buffering acceptable as long as final latency meets SLO?
4) Any regulatory constraints on quantized model weights / private data residency?

Next steps from our side:
- I'll share a short recommended cost/performance levers doc and a ballpark Dedicated sizing (GPU families, concurrency targets).
- If you confirm the items above, we'll propose: continuous batching + prefix caching, a quantization profile evaluation, and two model variants (low-latency & high-quality) with automatic fallback.

Attaching your SLO notes that you shared in the call for reference (nova_perf_slo_requirements.pdf).

Thanks -
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Evan Turner <evan.turner@novaretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@novaretail.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - post-call recap

Hi Neha - thanks for the clear recap. A few answers below: we copied Sofia for confirmation.

1) P95 target is end-to-end as measured by our edge service (so includes network + model). We can instrument with a header if useful.
2) Token distribution for the recommender prompt (examples attached in the doc): p50 ~ 600 tokens, p95 ~ 1,150 tokens. During promo spikes we see a heavier tail.
3) Streaming is preferred for UX - ideally first token < 120ms for web clients, but if you can guarantee final p95 < 200ms server-side buffering is acceptable as fallback.
4) No special constraints on quantization; data residency: US only for production.

We also added a short performance note: during the last holiday promo we saw concurrency hit ~180 at peak for a short window (20-30 mins). Budget is flexible if you can demonstrate cost per 1k requests under X (we'll share target offline).

Evan
Director, Platform Engineering | Nova Retail
evan.turner@novaretail.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Turner <evan.turner@novaretail.com>, Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@novaretail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Performance SLO qualification - post-call recap

Marissa / Rishi - forwarding the confirmed SLOs from Nova (p95 end-to-end <200ms, first token <120ms preferred, p95 tokens ~1150 during spikes, peak concurrency ~180). Key asks: propose cost/performance levers to hit these SLOs while keeping unit cost reasonable.

Quick asks for the proposal:
- Can you draft a 1-page options matrix (attached: redwood_latency_options.xlsx) covering:
  * Dedicated GPU families (A100 vs H100 equivalents) and expected p95 latency for the token distribution
  * Continuous batching parameters (batch window ms, max batch size) and expected throughput gains
  * Prefix/KV caching options and approx hit-rate assumptions for recommendation use-case
  * Quantization profiles we'd recommend (8-bit, 4-bit where feasible) and expected perf/cost delta
  * Model variants: low-latency truncated/quantized variant vs high-quality full precision variant, and fallback strategy

- Please include an estimated Dedicated pool sizing (number of GPUs, concurrency per GPU) and a conservative throughput/cost estimate (cost per 1k requests). Evan - if you have a target cost-per-1k we should aim for, please share and we'll tune assumptions.

PTA: I'll coordinate a quick follow-up demo next week if that helps - 30 minutes to walk through the options.

-Neha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Turner <evan.turner@novaretail.com>, Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@novaretail.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - post-call recap

Hi team - thanks Neha, Evan for the clear context. High-level proposed levers to meet p95 <200ms (for ~1k tokens typical; p95 up to ~1.2k tokens during spikes):

1) Serving & GPU selection
- Recommend starting with H100-class instances for headroom on concurrency during promo spikes (these give best latency for long sequences). For cost-sensitive pilots we can run a small A100-class pool + low-latency model variant.

2) Continuous batching configuration
- Batch window: 6-12ms for web UI flows (lower for streaming), max batch size tuned to GPU memory (we estimate 32-64 tokens/batch equivalently ~8-16 requests per batch for your token distribution).
- Benefit: 25-45% throughput improvement while preserving p95 latency when window <=12ms.

3) Prefix/KV caching
- Recommendation: enable prefix caching for user history/contexts that repeat across sessions. Expect conservative hit rate 15-30% for recommender prompts with templated context; hit-rate reduces effective tokens and lowers latency/cost.

4) Quantization profiles & model variants
- Two variants suggested:
  a) Low-latency variant: 4-bit quantized, distillation-tuned model for same task with small accuracy delta - first token latency reduced by ~30-45%. Good for primary route during spikes.
  b) High-quality variant: 8-bit quantized or fp16 full-quality model for fallbacks or critical flows.
- Redwood can run an eval comparing quality delta on your eval set; recommend a short A/B test (10% traffic) to validate.

5) Streaming & first-token optimization
- For <120ms first-token UX target: enable partial decoding + token-priority scheduling on the runtime; this will get first byte out faster at slight throughput cost. Use for web clients only; mobile can use buffered responses.

6) Autoscaling & fallback policies
- Configure autoscale with burst capacity (20%) and a policy to fallback from high-quality to low-latency variant if p95 starts to breach SLA. Also route to a regional pool if US pool saturates.

Estimated sizing (ballpark):
- Pilot (50 concurrent steady, 180 peak): 4 x H100-class GPUs with 18-24 concurrency per GPU (continuous batching + caching).
- Cost: conservative estimate $Y per 1k requests (see attached spreadsheet redwood_latency_options.xlsx for assumptions). We will refine once we have token-distribution telemetry and your cost target.

Action items / next steps:
- Neha: schedule 30m follow-up demo next week (I can present the latency options and a quick A/B plan).
- Evan: share the target cost-per-1k you mentioned offline so we can tune quantization & GPU choice to meet it.
- Marissa / Rishi: I'll prepare an A/B test plan and tie the rollout to automatic fallback policies.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through specifics.

Best -
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
